oauthOidc.title: OAuth 2.0 / OIDC
oauthOidc.subtitle: Authorization Code + PKCE · fixture preview
oauthOidc.outcome: Understand the roles, browser redirects and server-side boundaries behind a secure sign-in journey.
oauthOidc.objective: Explain how a browser, confidential client and provider work together, and why API authorization is a separate decision.

user.label: Human user
user.description: The person initiating the journey. The human, rather than the SPA, is the Resource Owner.

browser.label: Browser / SPA
browser.description: Displays the playground and follows browser redirects. It is not the OAuth client in this architecture.

bff.label: NestJS BFF
bff.description: The proposed confidential client owns transactions, server-held tokens and the application session. No backend is connected to this preview.

authorization-server.label: Authorization Server
authorization-server.description: Handles authorization requests and code exchange. This logical role shares the Keycloak deployment with the Identity Provider.

identity-provider.label: Identity Provider
identity-provider.description: Authenticates the user in Keycloak’s UI. This is a logical role, not a second deployed server or an original OAuth 2.0 role.

resource-server.label: Resource Server
resource-server.description: Independently validates the Access Token and permissions before returning synthetic data in a future runnable mission.

roles.title: Understand the actors
roles.explanation: Separate the human user, browser, OAuth client, Authorization Server, Identity Provider and Resource Server. Two Keycloak roles share one deployment.

authorization.title: Follow the front channel
authorization.explanation: In a real flow, the BFF initiates a redirect and the browser navigates to Keycloak. This preview never starts authentication or leaves for a provider.

identity.title: Locate authentication
identity.explanation: Credentials belong in Keycloak’s login experience. The playground does not provide a password form or observe provider-internal authentication.

exchange.title: Examine the back channel
exchange.explanation: The BFF correlates the callback, exchanges the code directly with Keycloak and validates the OIDC response. A successful exchange would not directly instrument Keycloak’s internal checks.

tokens.title: Distinguish token purposes
tokens.explanation: An ID Token conveys the authentication result to the client. An Access Token is used at the Resource Server. Neither belongs in this inspector.

resource.title: Find the API boundary
resource.explanation: A session alone does not prove API authorization. The Resource Server must check the intended audience, issuer, lifetime, trust and permission.

evidence.title: Review evidence limits
evidence.explanation: Load the fixture samples to explore safe explanatory fields. None is an observed trace; no authentication, API permission or session outcome is demonstrated.

preview.note: Fixture-only preview. Samples explain a possible journey; no network operation, authentication or session is created.

authorization-example.title: Browser authorization redirect
authorization-example.summary: An example of the browser following a BFF-initiated redirect to the Authorization Server. No redirect occurred.
authorization-example.explanation: The BFF is the OAuth client. It creates the authorization transaction; the browser carries the request to Keycloak. A learning checkpoint cannot pause or execute this redirect.

provider-internal-example.title: Provider-internal PKCE binding
provider-internal-example.summary: A teaching note about a provider-internal check, not an instrumented event.
provider-internal-example.explanation: The Authorization Server checks the verifier against the original challenge during code exchange. A BFF could observe the exchange outcome, but cannot claim a direct trace of this internal check.

exchange-example.title: Direct code exchange
exchange-example.summary: An example of direct BFF-to-provider communication. No exchange or session was created.
exchange-example.explanation: The BFF exchanges the authorization code and validates the OIDC response before establishing a session. Tokens stay server-side. This fixture contains no code, verifier, token response, or session result.

resource-example.title: Independent resource authorization
resource-example.summary: An example of a protected-resource boundary. No resource request was sent or permitted.
resource-example.explanation: A Resource Server independently validates trust, issuer, audience, lifetime and permission for an Access Token. An ID Token describes an authentication result for the client and is not an API access credential.

epa.title: ePA / gematik
epa.subtitle: Protected-system boundaries · conceptual layout
epa.outcome: Explore a conceptual map of identity, authorization and protected-system responsibilities in an ePA journey.
epa.objective: Test how different actors and security boundaries fit the workspace. Exact protocol choreography is a future specification decision.

insured-person.label: Insured person
insured-person.description: Illustrative initiator of a protected ePA journey. No real patient or medical data is used.

fdv.label: FdV / client
fdv.description: Illustrative user-facing access channel. This layout does not imply an implemented browser-based FdV.

sectoral-idp.label: Sectoral IdP
sectoral-idp.description: Illustrative authentication or federation responsibility, when applicable to a future specified scenario.

epa-authorization.label: ePA Authorization Service
epa-authorization.description: A conceptual authorization boundary. No ePA authorization operation is implemented or demonstrated.

vau.label: ePA system / VAU
vau.description: A protected subsystem and secure-communication topic to model separately. No live TI connection, exact sequence, or certification is claimed.

actors.title: Discover responsibilities
actors.explanation: These actor types test the layout. They do not imply that every actor participates in one sequence or that a specific ePA scenario has been implemented.

identity.title: Examine identity boundaries
identity.explanation: Identify where identity or federation responsibilities could belong. Current applicable gematik specifications must determine the future scenario.

authorization.title: Inspect authorization boundaries
authorization.explanation: Identity and authorization responsibilities are distinct. This conceptual map specifies no requests, decisions, credentials or operational results.

protected.title: Understand protected systems
protected.explanation: A protected subsystem and secure-communication boundary need their own specification. No VAU behavior is simulated here.

evidence.title: Separate concept from evidence
evidence.explanation: There is no live integration, telemetry or simulated operational result. The empty timeline is intentional. This preview makes no gematik compliance or certification claim.

preview.note: Planned — no live integration, telemetry or simulated operational results. Actor placement is conceptual and does not define a protocol sequence.

catalog.heading: Understand the flow.
catalog.intro: Explore authentication and authorization through actors, explanations and safe evidence. Choose a preview to enter Mission Control.
catalog.noticeTitle: A place to explore, with honest evidence.
catalog.notice: These previews use fixture content. No sign-in, protected API call or live protocol integration runs here. Planned missions stay planned until their real execution is verified.

principles.label: How Mission Control works
principles.actors: Understand who is responsible for each part of a journey.
principles.explanation: Explore checkpoints at your pace, independent of execution.
principles.evidence: Separate what can be observed from what is being explained.

workspace.checkpointNote: Checkpoint selection is learning navigation. It does not execute a flow.
workspace.context: Select an actor, checkpoint or fixture sample to explore its context.

announcements.loaded: Fixture samples loaded. No live operation occurred.
announcements.replayed: Explanation replayed from the first fixture sample.
announcements.reset: View reset. Loaded fixture samples are preserved.
announcements.fitted: Map at readable size. Scroll horizontally to reach additional participants.

runtime.notice: Private integration for verification. The BFF holds OAuth credentials; Keycloak supplies the login screen. Provider-internal password checks, PKCE comparison and token creation remain explained, not observable. Catalog availability is still unverified.
runtime.catalogNotice: Fixture and conceptual previews remain available. The separately configured private integration is for verification; runnable catalog availability is not yet released.
runtime.traceUnavailable: Trace incomplete or unavailable. Existing eligible observations are retained where possible; no missing event is invented.

authentication.expired: Application authentication: expired. Start a fresh attempt.
authentication.unavailable: Application authentication: unavailable until status is restored.

run.none: No current run. Start authentication to create a fresh attempt.
run.pending: Current login attempt: pending. Return or retry; no provider success is inferred.
run.authenticated: Current login attempt: authenticated. Resource authorization is checked separately.
run.provider-denied: Current login attempt: provider denial. Retry creates a fresh attempt.
run.authentication-failed: Current login attempt: failed. No upstream diagnostics are displayed.
run.signed-out: Locally signed out. Eligible safe history remains inspectable; provider SSO may still exist.
run.cancelled: Current login attempt: cancelled. Retry creates a fresh transaction.
run.expired: Current run: expired. Viewing history does not renew its lifetime.

errors.unavailable: The private backend is unavailable. Refresh status or start again when it is reachable.
errors.unsupported-response: Unsupported or unsafe response rejected. No raw data is displayed.
errors.ownership-lost: The owned run is unavailable or expired. Start a fresh attempt.
errors.capacity: Run capacity is unavailable. Start a fresh attempt; local sign-out remains independent.
errors.request-rejected: The request was rejected. Refresh status to recover the current browser context.
errors.timeout: The request timed out. Its completion is unknown; refresh status before continuing.

resource.allowed: Last resource outcome: synthetic Basic/playground-demo read allowed.
resource.permission-denied: Last resource outcome: Resource Server authorization denied (HTTP 403). Application authentication is separate.
resource.token-denied: Last resource outcome: Resource Server rejected its credential (HTTP 401). Application authentication is separate.
resource.local-rejection: Last resource outcome: rejected locally by the BFF. This is not a HAPI denial.
resource.timeout: Last resource outcome: timed out. No Resource Server denial is inferred.
resource.network-error: Last resource outcome: transport unavailable. No Resource Server decision is inferred.
resource.unexpected-status: Last resource outcome: unexpected HTTP response. No internal cause is inferred.
resource.invalid-response: Last resource outcome: response rejected by the BFF safe projection.
resource.response-too-large: Last resource outcome: response exceeded the safe size limit.
resource.unavailable: Last resource result unavailable to this view. No server decision is inferred.

authorization-started.title: Authorization started
authorization-started.summary: The BFF created a fresh standard login attempt.
authorization-started.explanation: This records local initiation, not receipt or authentication at the provider.

authorization-redirect-issued.title: Authorization redirect issued
authorization-redirect-issued.summary: The BFF issued a browser redirect toward the Authorization Server.
authorization-redirect-issued.explanation: This is the BFF → browser instruction. It does not prove the provider received the navigation.

authorization-failed.title: Authorization preparation failed
authorization-failed.summary: The BFF could not prepare the authorization attempt.
authorization-failed.explanation: Only the bounded local failure is known. No provider-internal cause is inferred.

authorization-cancelled.title: Authorization attempt cancelled
authorization-cancelled.summary: The BFF cancelled this context-bound attempt.
authorization-cancelled.explanation: A superseding attempt, logout or expiry can cancel work. A retry creates a new transaction.

callback-accepted.title: Callback correlated
callback-accepted.summary: The BFF accepted a response correlated to the owning browser.
callback-accepted.explanation: Correlation is checked before one-time consumption and code exchange. It does not by itself establish authentication.

callback-rejected.title: Callback rejected locally
callback-rejected.summary: The BFF rejected an owned callback attempt.
callback-rejected.explanation: The reason is a safe classification. No raw callback or provider error text is exposed.

token-exchange-started.title: Code exchange started
token-exchange-started.summary: The BFF initiated the code-exchange attempt.
token-exchange-started.explanation: The confidential client uses server-held credentials and the stored PKCE verifier on the back channel.

token-response-received.title: Token response received
token-response-received.summary: The BFF received the expected HTTP token response.
token-response-received.explanation: Receipt is distinct from token validation. Neither tokens nor the response body are teaching evidence.

token-exchange-failed.title: Code exchange failed
token-exchange-failed.summary: The BFF could not complete the exchange successfully.
token-exchange-failed.explanation: The recorded status or classification describes the BFF result, not an observed provider-internal check.

token-validation-started.title: OIDC validation started
token-validation-started.summary: The BFF started validating the OIDC response and ID Token.
token-validation-started.explanation: These are local client checks. This event does not assert that every check has already passed.

token-validation-succeeded.title: OIDC validation succeeded
token-validation-succeeded.summary: The BFF completed its OIDC response and ID Token validation.
token-validation-succeeded.explanation: Client-side validation is distinct from independent Access Token authorization at the Resource Server.

token-validation-failed.title: OIDC validation rejected
token-validation-failed.summary: The BFF rejected the OIDC response or ID Token.
token-validation-failed.explanation: No session is established from this attempt. The UI does not expose claims or guess the failed internal check.

session-established.title: Application session established
session-established.summary: The BFF committed an authenticated session and rotated browser context.
session-established.explanation: This follows validation and the final eligibility check. It does not grant FHIR access by itself.

workspace-redirect-issued.title: Workspace return issued
workspace-redirect-issued.summary: The BFF issued the clean redirect to this OAuth Workspace.
workspace-redirect-issued.explanation: The fixed return contains no callback secrets. Viewing the Workspace restores state without repeating protocol work.

session-ended.title: Local session ended
session-ended.summary: The BFF completed local sign-out or authentication expiry.
session-ended.explanation: Eligible safe history can remain inspectable. This does not claim provider SSO logout or bearer-token revocation.

resource-requested.title: Synthetic read initiated
resource-requested.summary: The BFF initiated the fixed synthetic resource read.
resource-requested.explanation: Only its server-held standard Access Token is used. This event does not claim receipt or approval by HAPI.

resource-response-received.title: Resource response received
resource-response-received.summary: The BFF received an actual HTTP response from the Resource Server.
resource-response-received.explanation: The BFF observes status and receipt time. Only an explicit validated report can state a server decision; internal checks remain unobserved.

resource-allowed.title: Synthetic read succeeded
resource-allowed.summary: The BFF accepted the allowed synthetic resource response.
resource-allowed.explanation: The bounded fictional result passed projection and current-session eligibility. Authentication and resource authorization are separate outcomes.

resource-denied.title: Resource denial received
resource-denied.summary: The BFF handled a real Resource Server authentication or authorization denial.
resource-denied.explanation: Inspect the received status and any explicit reported reason. The BFF application session may still be authenticated.

resource-rejected.title: Resource access rejected locally
resource-rejected.summary: The BFF rejected resource access because eligible application authentication was absent.
resource-rejected.explanation: This is a BFF-local decision. It is never evidence of a HAPI request or denial; separately received responses retain their own provenance.

resource-failed.title: Resource operation unavailable
resource-failed.summary: The BFF could not complete the bounded resource operation.
resource-failed.explanation: A transport or response failure is distinct from an observed Resource Server denial. No hidden root cause or body is exposed.
